goal: Stack the three blocks (that differ in texture) on top of each other into one tower, then return the arm(s) to the start pose.
instruction_templates: Stack the three blocks with different textures.
success: is_stacked, label_list=[block_0, block_1, block_2], in_order=False, xy_threshold chosen per episode from block_0's model index: 0.015 m for the small size group (indices 5,8,11,14,17), 0.0175 m for the medium group (6,9,12,15,18), 0.02 m for the large group (7,10,13,16,19), no z_threshold: the three block ROOT positions are sorted by height (z); for each vertically adjacent pair, horizontal (XY) root-to-root distance <= the xy threshold AND z gap (upper minus lower root z) >= 0.005 m (no upper bound). Any stacking order of the three blocks is accepted (the order is determined by their heights).

all_robot_back_to_origin: every target arm's end-effector pose is within 0.15 m per axis (|dx|,|dy|,|dz| each <= 0.15 m) and within 20 degrees (quaternion angular distance) of its start-of-episode pose (the arms must be returned to roughly their starting pose).
evaluation: Success conditions form ONE stage: after every action (once all simulation sub-steps of that action are done) the reward manager evaluates all conditions; the episode succeeds as soon as ALL hold simultaneously at the same moment (reward 1 -> episode ends with success). Conditions are not latched or ordered. Otherwise the episode ends as a failure after step_lim=550 actions (the check made after the last action still counts). No early-fail rule exists apart from the environment being flagged invalid (e.g. a required label missing / physics broken).
objects: block_0, block_1, block_2: three different instances of 'block' drawn without replacement from ONE randomly chosen size group (size0 indices 5,8,11,14,17; size1 6,9,12,15,18; size2 7,10,13,16,19), distinguished by texture ; 3 total, random positions on table x in [-0.45, 0.45], y in [-0.25, 0.0] (Table-relative), no random rotation; prohibited area [0.1,-0.23,-0.17,-0.1] is excluded
needs_memory_or_language: none (the instruction is the same fixed sentence; no target block is named, any order of stacking is accepted)
end_requirements: All target (controlled) arms must be back near their start pose when success is evaluated (it is one of the success conditions, see success list): every target arm's end-effector position within 0.15 m on EACH of x, y, z (per-axis, not Euclidean) and orientation within 20 degrees of its pose at the start of the episode (pose recorded right after the robot is set to its initial state). Gripper opening is NOT checked by the success test.
notes: The size group is hierarchical-random per episode, so block size (and, for stack_blocks, the xy tolerance 0.015/0.0175/0.02 m) varies per episode; all three blocks in an episode share the same size. Tolerance grows with block size: larger blocks are more forgiving. No gripper-open requirement in success. A process score (15 when gripper open (>=0.8 normalised) and at least one pair stacked; 100 for the full stack with gripper open) exists but does not decide success. Success is evaluated on object root poses/points, not on gripper contact. Object geometry sizes/asset dimensions are not in the source and cannot be determined statically.
